decisions.name: 286U real-line a.e. convergence
decisions.reason: The assigned Carleson A page supplies maximal bounds; the existing later FR-5 page owns the convergence implication. This full argument was inspected only to check the alleged strong-L2 supplier.
decisions.evidence: Step-8 lead scope review, 2026-09-11. Read Fremlin 286U including (a)-(c), printed pp.113-114: this is almost-everywhere convergence/identification of the real-line L2 transform. Current batch-5 A inventory supplies maximal estimates; thm-carleson-maximal-operator-is-strong-ltwo steps 1.1-4.1 use local restricted-weak interpolation and Schwartz density, not 286U. The later plan page divergence-and-almost-everywhere-convergence-of-fourier-series (288.14018, after 288.140175) contains the published conditional closure lem-fourier-maximal-weak-bound-closes-almost-everywhere-convergence. That torus result is not claimed to be a proof of the distinct real-line 286U statement. The source result remains outside this assigned maximal-bound inventory.

decisions.name: 286V torus L2 a.e. convergence
decisions.reason: Its full inspected kernel-comparison argument proves a.e. convergence for L2, not the claimed all-p maximal periodisation theorem. Retain as evidence of a design source mismatch, not as the missing transfer proof.
decisions.evidence: Step-8 lead scope review, 2026-09-11. Read the complete Fremlin 286V proof, printed pp.114-115: zero extension, inverse L2 transform and comparison of sine/Dirichlet kernels prove torus L2 a.e. convergence. The claim is neither a strong Lp maximal estimate nor the all-p transfer. Current lem-carleson-real-line-to-torus-transfer instead proves the conditional all-p transfer in steps 1.1-4.1 using Schwartz windows, half-integer cutoffs, periodic averaging and Fejer approximation; thm-carleson-hunt-maximal-inequality-on-the-torus applies that exact interface. The mismatch is retained as source-scope evidence, not used as a missing proof.

decisions.name: 286 Notes: Lp maximal estimates cited beyond the proof
decisions.reason: Bibliographic orientation lists Hunt and other sources but does not prove the all-p maximal estimate. It cannot discharge the assigned Hunt or transfer lemmas.
decisions.evidence: Step-8 lead scope review, 2026-09-11. Read Fremlin §286 Notes and comments, printed pp.115-116: the text says its methods do not reach the stated Lp extensions and lists references for the all-p maximal bound. Current thm-carleson-maximal-operator-is-strong-ltwo and thm-carleson-hunt-maximal-inequality-on-the-torus explicitly use local estimates at exponents r<p<s and model reconstruction, not bibliographic remarks as a proof. Keeping the notes as orientation preserves the source qualification and the actual maximal-bound contract.

decisions.name: 10.68: compact implies bounded
decisions.reason: Local compact convention includes boundedness; no consumer needs the converse for arbitrary linear maps.
decisions.evidence: The current weak-mixing and Chacon contracts use bounded operators directly and contain no dependency on the general compact-implies-bounded proposition.
